purpose: Regression fixture for finding lifecycle management — validates that historical findings are not treated as current governance conditions without revalidation against canonical state
invariant: A historical finding must never be treated as a current governance condition without revalidation against current authoritative state

source_incident.condition: seed contamination — platform migration initialized Librarian cursor from workbench seed

test_cases.name: finding_detected_is_current
test_cases.description: A newly detected finding is classified as current and actionable

test_cases.name: remediation_applied_through_authority_path
test_cases.description: A remediation receipt exists proving the finding was addressed through the governance authority path

test_cases.name: stale_finding_not_treated_as_current
test_cases.description: A finding whose underlying condition has been remediated must not be treated as a current governance condition, even if the detection state has not been updated

expected_outcome.reason: remediation evidence exists but detection state has not been revalidated against current canonical state

test_cases.name: revalidation_resolves_stale_finding
test_cases.description: Revalidation against current canonical state resolves a stale finding when remediation evidence is confirmed

test_cases.name: historical_finding_preserved_after_resolution
test_cases.description: A resolved finding retains its full forensic history — detection, severity, condition, remediation evidence, and resolution

test_cases.name: remediation_without_evidence_does_not_resolve
test_cases.description: A finding is not resolved merely because time passed or a remediation was attempted — resolution requires evidence of canonical state change

expected_outcome.reason: no remediation evidence; time elapsed does not constitute resolution

test_cases.name: three_state_layer_distinction
test_cases.description: The system correctly distinguishes canonical state, detection state, and reconciliation input — and identifies when detection state is stale relative to canonical state

expected_outcome.recommended_action: revalidate detection state against canonical state before consuming in reconciliation

invariant_tests.statement: A historical finding must never be treated as a current governance condition without revalidation against current authoritative state
Resolution requires evidence of canonical state change, not merely elapsed time
Resolved findings retain full forensic history including detection severity, condition, remediation evidence, and resolution timestamp

design_principles.evidence_based_not_timestamp_based: A finding should not become resolved merely because enough time passed. It should become resolved because current authoritative state + remediation evidence + fresh re-evaluation → resolution determination.
design_principles.measurement_not_intention: Measure what happened, rather than what was intended. A remediation occurring does not mean the remediation worked — both require subsequent measurement.
design_principles.observation_is_not_authority: The reconciliation system detects and classifies; it does not silently mutate canonical state. Resolution requires Owner authority.
design_principles.historical_finding_preservation: Historical findings are forensic evidence. They are preserved with full lifecycle metadata, not deleted when resolved.
